title: synthetic-scenario-orchestrator-runbook-2026
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Purpose

This runbook documents the operator procedures and automation patterns for running synthetic scenario orchestrations against Redwood platform services. The goal is to provide a repeatable, low-risk way to validate SLOs, exercise fallback logic, and generate reproducible telemetry for post-test analysis. Use this document for scheduled verification runs, pre-release canaries, and incident replay drills.

Scope

- Services in scope: traffic-sim, orchestration-service, tenant-router, prefix-cache, kv-cache-shard-manager, telemetry-fanout, model-proxy
- Tests covered: latency tail simulation, token-burst load, partial region failure injection, model-variant fallback verification, cache-coherent eviction scenarios
- Environments: staging, pre-prod, and synthetic-lab (not production unless explicitly approved)

Owner and Contacts

- Primary owner: eng-platform (on-call rotation: platform-operator)
- Runbook maintainer: Aisha Raman (eng-platform)
- Pager contacts: platform-oncall@redwood.com, eng-sre-runbook-cust@redwood.com

SLOs and Acceptance Criteria

- P95 request latency for traffic-sim control path: < 120ms
- P99 request latency for tenant-router during normal synthetic load: < 350ms
- Error rate (5m window) must remain < 0.5% for critical routes; if breached, abort and escalate
- Token surge handling: system must shed non-priority tenants with grace and maintain 90% success for priority tenants

Prerequisites and Safety Controls

1) Authorization: operator must have role platform-operator or platform-admin in IAM; confirm with `rbac-cli whoami`
2) Environment locks: ensure environment is tagged in the orchestration service as `synthetic-enabled:true`
3) Blacklist: verify customer-sensitive tenants are excluded from tenant lists via `/etc/synthetic/tenant_exclude.yml`
4) Default kill-switch: `orchestration-service/synthetic:abort` feature flag in feature-store (used by tests to emergency-stop)

Architecture (high level)

The orchestrator uses a controller pattern: a coordinator job in `orchestration-service` generates scenario steps and uses `traffic-sim` agents (deployed per-region) to drive HTTP and streaming requests through `tenant-router`. Observability is captured via `telemetry-fanout` which emits cost, latency, and error metrics to the observability pipeline. KV cache interactions are exercised through `kv-cache-shard-manager` to validate cache-coherency.

Diagram (text)

coord-job -> orchestration-service -> traffic-sim agents -> tenant-router -> model-proxy -> runtime (kv/prefix-cache)
                                 \-> telemetry-fanout -> observability pipeline

Run Types (examples)

- Baseline: low-intensity, verifies measurement pipelines and drains any residual state
- Burst: short 60s token-burst at 5x normal traffic profile to validate shedding behavior
- Degradation: inject higher tail latencies at model-proxy layer and verify fallback to variant model and region
- Eviction: incremental cache-eviction simulation to validate prefix-cache rehydration and warmup

Operational Playbook (step-by-step)

1) Pre-run checklist (operator)
  a) Confirm environment: `kubectl --context synthetic-lab get namespace synthetic-ops`
  b) Load excluded-tenant list: `cat /etc/synthetic/tenant_exclude.yml` and verify 
  c) Ensure observability pipelines green: check `dashboards/synthetic-pipeline-health` (green for last 30m)
  d) Notify stakeholders: post to #platform-tests Slack channel with run ID and scope

2) Start a Baseline run (quick smoke)\
  a) Create a run ID: `RUN_ID=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M)-smoke`
  b) Launch: `orchestrator-cli start --run $RUN_ID --profile baseline --env synthetic-lab`
  c) Verify agents: `orchestrator-cli agents --run $RUN_ID` (expect: 3 agents online per-region)
  d) Monitor dashboards: `dashboards/synthetic-baseline/$RUN_ID` for latency/error trends

3) Execute a Burst run (60s token surge)
  a) `orchestrator-cli start --run $RUN_ID --profile burst --duration 60s --intensity 5x`
  b) Watch for token-cost attribution spike on `dashboards/token-burst/$RUN_ID` and ensure priority tenant success >= 90%
  c) If error-rate > 0.5% for critical routes -> `orchestrator-cli abort --run $RUN_ID` and follow escalation below

4) Degradation run with fallback verification
  a) Use fault injector to throttle model-proxy: `fault-injector inject --target model-proxy --latency 500ms --p99 1s --duration 120s --run $RUN_ID`
  b) Validate that orchestration-service applies fallback policy to use variant `gptx-qa-2` and route priority-tenants to region fallback
  c) Confirm telemetry entries: `telemetry-query --run $RUN_ID --filter "fallback=true"` (should show > 95% successful fallbacks)

5) Eviction and cache-coherency test
  a) Trigger eviction: `kv-cli evict-prefix --prefix test-prefix --shard all --run $RUN_ID`
  b) Monitor warmup: `dashboards/cache-warmup/$RUN_ID` and ensure rehydration p95 < 500ms for affected prefixes

Abort and Escalation Criteria

- Safety abort: any run where a blacklisted tenant receives traffic -> instant abort and page SRE (pagerduty: ENG-SRE-PLATFORM)
- Observability break: if telemetry pipeline fails to export metrics for > 5m -> abort and open internal incident
- SLO breach: see SLOs above; on breach, collect traces and escalate to oncall and responsible service owner

Escalation Steps

1) Run abort: `orchestrator-cli abort --run $RUN_ID`
2) Gather artifacts: `artifact-collector collect --run $RUN_ID --dest /tmp/$RUN_ID-artifacts`
3) Open incident: use incident-template `synthetic-run-breach` and include artifacts link

Automated Verification and Post-Run Tasks

- After successful completion, the orchestrator will upload a run manifest and telemetry snapshot to `s3://redwood-synthetic-runs/$RUN_ID/manifest.json`
- Operators must run `orchestrator-cli verify --run $RUN_ID` which runs automated checks (metric thresholds, fallback counts, agent health) and returns `PASS` or `FAIL`
- For FAIL results, attach `run_id` to a retrospective template and schedule a 30-minute triage within 24 hours

Example Config Snippet (orchestration manifest)

---
run_id: "20260301-0900-burst"
profile: "burst"
duration: "60s"
intensity: "5x"
env: "synthetic-lab"
agents:
  per_region: 3
  types: [http-stream, websocket, grpc]
exclusions:
  tenants_from_file: "/etc/synthetic/tenant_exclude.yml"
safety:
  abort_flag: "orchestration-service/synthetic:abort"
  backoff_policy: "stepwise-10s-60s"
---

Observability and Dashboards

- Primary dashboard: dashboards/synthetic-overview (latency heatmap, error rates, fallback counts, token-cost attribution)
- Secondary: dashboards/telemetry-health, dashboards/cache-warmup, dashboards/token-burst
- Traces: query `service:tenant-router` with tag `synthetic_run:$RUN_ID`

Runbook Testing and Maintenance

- Runbook audit cadence: quarterly (owner: eng-platform)
- Every major change to orchestration-service must include an automated synthetic run in CI (see `ci/orchestration/synthetic-verify.yml`)
- Postmortem requirement: any test that required manual operator intervention must produce a retrospective within 72 hours

Checklist (quick reference)

- [ ] Confirm RBAC and environment lock
- [ ] Load excluded tenants file
- [ ] Notify #platform-tests and stakeholders
- [ ] Start baseline smoke run
- [ ] Start scheduled run and monitor dashboards
- [ ] Abort if any blacklisted tenant receives traffic or SLOs breach
- [ ] Run automated verification and collect artifacts
- [ ] Create retrospective if FAIL or manual intervention occurred

Retrospective Notes (template prompts)

- What happened (sequence)?
- What indicators were most helpful?
- What automation gaps existed?
- Action items with owners and deadlines

Appendix: Useful Commands

- List active runs: `orchestrator-cli list --active`
- Get run details: `orchestrator-cli describe --run $RUN_ID --output yaml`
- Abort run: `orchestrator-cli abort --run $RUN_ID`
- Collect artifacts: `artifact-collector collect --run $RUN_ID --dest /tmp/$RUN_ID-artifacts`
- Verify run: `orchestrator-cli verify --run $RUN_ID`
